Therefore, when Nur al-Din wrote to him,
"Behold, I am encamping against Kerak;
you also, without delay, gather your forces and arrive there,"
Saladin was afraid and did not go.
And on account of this Nur al-Din became enraged,
and he wanted to enter Egypt in person and expel him from there.
Then Saladin assembled the nobles who were with him,
and took counsel with them
as to how the policy should be.
And while all of them were silent,
and did not know what to say—
rebellion or submission?—a youth arose, Saladin's nephew, and said:
"If Nur al-Din comes, we will fight with him,
and we will not allow him to enter Egypt."
And likewise also the rest of the youths, his companions, spoke.
Then Saladin's father and also his maternal uncle became angry,
and his father rebuked those youths.
And he said to Saladin:
"Is there really, among all these nobles, anyone who desires your welfare like me
and like this uncle of yours?" And he answered:
"No."
And he said: "Believe [me],
that if I or this uncle of yours see Nur al-Din,
we have nothing [to do] but dismount and kiss the ground before him.
And while we are like this,
who is there among these who, when he sees Nur al-Din,
would draw a sword in his face? And since all these territories of Egypt and beyond belong to Nur al-Din,
if he wishes to dismiss you from the governorship,
what need does he have to come against you with armies? Rather, let him send just a single person with two lines [of writing],
who will put a rope around your neck and drag you all the way to Damascus,
and set over his territory whomever he pleases!"
And that old man, Najm al-Din Ayyub, arose from his place,
and rebuked all the nobles and said:
"Arise!
All of us are servants of Nur al-Din,
and whatever he wishes, he will do with us."
And when they left and went away,
that old man said to Saladin:
"You are a youth without sense and confused of conduct.
Do you not know
that when Nur al-Din hears that you have rebelled against him,
he will abandon every affair
and pursue you until he uproots you? And who among the soldiers would abandon him
and follow you? And immediately these words which you have spoken will reach him by all means.
